I don't hand out quiz answers, even on a retake you'll "read up on later" — that's exactly the case this rule is for, since the point of the quiz is to measure what you can do without help. I'll coach you through it instead.

Look at what's actually going wrong in that scenario: the agent is stuck in a loop, repeating the same failing edit, and burning context on steps that aren't helping. For each option, ask yourself: **does this change address repetition, or does it just give the agent more of what it already has too much of?**

A useful way to sort them: some options make the loop capable of running *longer* or *harder* in the same failing pattern. Some options make the loop *stop* and hand control back when it's not making progress. Only one kind is a safeguard against a stuck loop — the other kind is just more rope.

Try explaining out loud, for each of the four options, what would actually happen to the next 10 steps if you made that change. You'll find that most of them either do nothing to the repetition or make it worse. Once you've done that, tell me which one you land on and why — I'll tell you if your reasoning holds up, just not which letter the key says.

Once this submission's graded, we can go through q3 properly.

What's your read on the four options — walk me through what each one would do to step 41?
